target_customer: Enterprise computer vision and ML teams, later industrial customers in mobility, security, logistics and manufacturing
problem: Labeling training data for computer vision is slow and expensive; Superb AI automates annotation and data curation across the ML lifecycle.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform plus professional services
product_category: Computer vision MLOps and data labeling platform

founders.name: Hyun Kim
education: Duke University, B.S. and Ph.D. dropout
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; the Feb 2021 release says he was on Forbes 2020 Under 30 Asia.

founders.background_notes: Named CTO in the 2021-02-02 PR Newswire release; the YC page lists a Jungkwon Lee.

founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without a bio.

founders.name: Jonghyuk Lee
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without a bio.

competitors.name: Labelbox
competitors.what: Collaborative training data platform for labeling and data management

competitors.name: Scale AI
competitors.what: API driven data labeling with a large contractor workforce
competitors.funding_then: $18M in August 2018, then $100M Series C in August 2019 (source dated a few months after the batch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Auto-labeling with few-shot models and a labeling platform required ML research plus product engineering for a small Seoul team in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Labeling tools were crowded and well funded, so differentiation depended on auto-label quality and later vision foundation models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded rivals dominated labeling; Superb AI shifted toward industrial video analytics and a vision foundation model by 2025 per its site.

market_need_then: Rapid growth in computer vision projects created heavy demand for labeled data; Scale and Labelbox raised large rounds in 2018 and 2019.

identity.visual_style: Dark technical style with stat callouts
identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and technical: 'Vision Intelligence for the Physical World'

brand_strength.rationale: Positive but generic name with a hyphenated domain; trademarks registered 2024 and 2025, but no brand press or community evidence.

pivots.from: Data labeling and MLOps platform for general computer vision
pivots.to: Industrial vision AI with video analytics and a vision foundation model
pivots.why: Company site now positions around industrial AI; no reason stated, date approximate from site and Forbes mention.

outcome_analysis: Superb AI raised a $9.3M Series A in February 2021, $16M Series B in September 2022 and $10.2M Series C in October 2024, reaching about $36.9M total by its own figure, with Korean strategic investors such as Doosan and Hyundai. It faces better funded labeling rivals, so it has repositioned toward industrial vision AI; smaller later rounds suggest it has not matched Scale-style growth.
notes: Total raised is $36.9M per the company's Series C post; the $11.3M cumulative after Series A implies about $2M earlier (seed with KT and Duke Angel Network) that was not found as its own round. CB Insights lists a Series C-II of $9.54M in December 2025 (single aggregator, unverified). Scale's $100M round dates to August 2019, after the Winter 2019 batch, so only the earlier $18M is as of founding. Pivot date is approximate.
